speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, please describe when these symptoms first started and if they have progressed over time. Additionally, have you experienced any changes in your handwriting, speech, or swallowing difficulties recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the "drunk" appearance of your walk and right-sided clumsiness suggests cerebellar involvement. To narrow this down, have you noticed any changes in your handwriting, slurred speech, or difficulty swallowing? Also, please tell me specifically when these symptoms first began.

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)

I am concerned that your history of Crohn's disease and your recent use of natalizumab may have predisposed you to PML, a severe infection of the brain that causes these neurological symptoms. Have you recently suffered any new headaches, vision changes, or confusion alongside your walking difficulties?
